---
description: "Use when creating or updating Japanese vocabulary flashcard decks from a pasted word list. Covers card data, back-only particle hints, original illustrations, unique progress storage, validation, and publishing."
---

# Vocabulary deck workflow

- Use `chapter21_words.html` as the working example for word decks. Keep its flashcard controls, responsive layout, and accessible SVG illustration pattern.
- Create a separate root-level file named `chapter<N>_words.html`. Update its browser title and visible heading for the requested chapter.
- Convert each supplied vocabulary row into one `INITIAL_CARDS` entry in the same order. Preserve Japanese spelling and readings. If the kanji column is blank, use the kana as `kanji` and `reading`. Preserve the supplied Estonian meaning.
- Keep particle hints out of `estonian`. Put them in the optional `particles` property so they appear only on the answer side. Render them below the Japanese reading and keep that element hidden when no hint exists.
- Give each card exactly one matching, original manga-inspired illustration in `WORD_ILLUSTRATIONS`, in the same order as `INITIAL_CARDS`. Keep the illustrations self-contained in the HTML (inline SVG/emoji; do not hotlink copyrighted manga or anime art).
- Use deck-specific `STORAGE_KEY` and `ORDER_STORAGE_KEY` values so study progress is independent of every other deck.
- Keep card IDs sequential from 1. Before finishing, verify the number and order of cards, one illustration per card, particle hints absent from front-side meanings, valid JavaScript, and correct answers/illustrations on representative cards.
- The root `index.html` is generated by `generate_index.py` from other root-level HTML files. Do not edit the generated menu manually. Run `python generate_index.py` to preview it; the GitHub Pages workflow regenerates it and publishes new decks on pushes to `main`.
- Leave existing decks untouched. Commit and push changes only when the user asks to upload, publish, or otherwise requests it.
